text:
sam: Heads-up — we're seeing sustained packet loss to the storage endpoint in us-west2b starting ~10m ago. GPU pods there show P99 infer latency creeping from 220ms -> 780ms. I'm going to start a scoped evacuation of non-critical pools (preemptible and batch) to reduce tail latency.
maria: How broad? all GPU pools in the AZ or only spot/preemptible?
sam: Starting with preemptible/spot only. No forced termination yet — doing a soft drain + evict only new jobs. Will keep a tiny warm pool for cache priming.
deploy-bot: trigger: drain-started zone=us-west2b pools=[gpu-preemptible, batch-gpu] started_by=sam
leo: +1 on soft drain. We should route new traffic away from us-west2b and keep steady-state failover to usw2a/c. Can infra-router do a weighted shift temporarily?
olivia: We can do a 40/10/50 shift (a/c/b) to bias away but keep some capacity for stateful caches. If we move too much the other AZs might hotspot.
kevin: Cost call: if we spin up on-demand in other AZs for backfill we'll incur extra spend — roughly estimated $6k/day for the additional nodes. Alternative is to throttle batch and keep latency-sensitive routes prioritized.
sanjay: Suggestion: execute the following in traffic-router: 
```
routectl set-weight --region=us-west2 --zone-weights "usw2a=0.45,usw2b=0.10,usw2c=0.45" --reason "us-west2b packet loss soft-evac"
```
That keeps a small percentage going to usw2b for warm caches but prevents new heavy allocations.
maria: Good. Also enable KV cache replication for the hot keys across A/C — otherwise cold starts will spike generation cost and latencies.
sam: Starting the routectl change now. Will also kick off drain in kube: 
```
kubectl annotate nodepool/gpu-preemptible-usw2b migration=softdrain-1876543210
kubectl cordon -l pool=gpu-preemptible,zone=usw2b
kubectl drain -l pool=gpu-preemptible,zone=usw2b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300 --force=false
```
deploy-bot: cordon/eviction queued for 18 nodes; progress=0/18
monitor-bot: alert: node-network-packetloss detected zone=usw2b severity=warning count=23 pkt_loss=6.7% avg_p99_latency=782ms
leo: If cordon+drain stalls, we should fallback to hard-provision in usw2a/c or enable Dedicated burst if we hit queue backed-off errors. Olivia — can you check Dedicated spare pool availability?
olivia: Dedicated spare cushion: 8 GPUs free in usw2a, 6 in usw2c. Can be reserved for 15m bursts. We should keep them as a last resort because of commit costs but fine as a short-term to avoid client errors.
kevin: Approve using Dedicated spare for 30m if we see ERROR: allocation failed in the scheduler. Please annotate costs to incident.
sanjay: Note: need to warm KV cache after nodes are up. Run this job to prewarm: `scripts/infra/prewarm_kv.sh --keys-file=hot_keys.txt --pool=usw2a` — schedule after routectl completes.
sam: Evictions at 5/18. No hot restarts observed yet. p99 on inference endpoints trending down to 320ms for redirected traffic.
maria: Keep an eye on tail. Also add a temporary scaling cap on long-running batch jobs: set batch.max_concurrent=60% of usual until we clear the zone.
oncall-bot: incident-created id=INC-2029-487 zone=us-west2b impact=partial-az-degradation owner=sam
leo: Small note — telemetry shows disk I/O retries spiking on a subset of nodes (iostat: await high). Could be local NIC or rack egress. If disk I/O is primary we should escalate to cloud provider network ops.
sam: I'll open a support ticket with provider. For now proceed with the soft-drain plan. If provider confirms hardware/networkivity we may need full AZ evacuate.
olivia: I'm running a dry-backfill in usw2a/c to validate client routing and cache warming — no costful reserve yet, just spinning ephemeral instances for readiness tests.
sam: Great. We'll reconvene in 20m or earlier if evictions fail or alerts escalate. +cc @maria @leo @olivia @kevin. :eyes:
maria: copying runbook steps into the thread: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/zonal-evac — follow Step 1-5 for soft-drain, Step 6 if doing full drain.
kevin: Logging cost note to finance: high-priority infra incident — potential $6k/day for on-demand backfill + Dedicated burst if used.
sam: Last update before handoff: evictions 12/18 complete, routectl weights applied, p99 down to 280ms for majority of traffic. Keeping small warm pool in usw2b (2 nodes). Monitoring closely, will update if we need Dedicated burst or provider escalation.
oncall-bot: incident-updated id=INC-2029-487 state=mitigating
maria: Thanks team. I'll keep the channel open and will call for a post-incident ops notes capture after we resolve. :thumbsup:
